svg.title: Peru ENSO Observatory architecture: simplified diagram
svg.desc: Official ENSO sources, hazard alerts and news feeds are fetched every night by three collectors: a machine in Peru (21:00), n8n in the cloud (22:50) and GitHub Actions (23:37), following a registry measured every Monday. When a source does not answer, the Peru and n8n copies, the Internet Archive or the previous publication are used. The Python pipeline reads, validates, places news by location and publishes everything at once; the site shows each value with links to the live source and the archived copy. Two watchdogs check the site every 6 hours and incidents become issues.
svg.text: Peru ENSO Observatory architecture: simplified diagram
Read it top to bottom. Box numbers follow the walkthrough below; line letters are the connections, explained at the end. Tags A1 to A10 open each part's annex: its steps, technologies and

g.title: A. Official sources and alerts → Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru): Downloaded every night. Every night the collectors download the official data and alerts. What only answers inside the country, like the ENFEN portal, is fetched by the computer in Peru.
B. News → Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru): News feeds. GitHub Actions reads the news on every run and n8n keeps a copy. Google News forbids robots: it is read like a feed reader, at most once a day.

C. Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru) → Daily pipeline: Data with its origin. Each value arrives with who downloaded it, from where and when. When the computer in Peru pushes its copy, it also asks for the site to be updated.

D. Backup → Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru): Internet Archive copy. If the source, its mirror and the Peru, n8n and console copies fail (and, for ENFEN documents, IMARPE's repository), the download uses the latest Internet Archive copy, with its date.

E. Backup → Daily pipeline: If a source fails. If a source does not answer today, its last good published value is used, with its real date. A missing news history is restored from the data-archive copy.
F. Daily pipeline → Publication: Checked data. Series, official statuses, the GRD signal, placed news and the list of problems go on to build the files people will see.
G. Publication → Website: Published and checked. The site is uploaded whole at once and then checked to make sure the live page shows the new version. If something serious failed, yesterday's stays.
H. Website → Backup: Today backs up tomorrow. What the site shows today is what tomorrow's run uses as the last good value if a source fails.
I. Daily pipeline → Backup: Permanent copy. After each good run, the new raw responses and the news history are saved in an archive that never deletes anything.

J. Publication → Places and documents console: Items to review. The console has the last 120 days of news and opens on doubtful places, so a person can confirm or fix them. It also lists the documents the run could not download.

K. Places and documents console → Daily pipeline: Place corrections. Corrections are applied in the next run and have the final say. If the console does not answer, the ones already published are used.

L. Places and documents console → Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru): PDF uploaded by hand. If no automatic route brings an official document, an administrator uploads it in the console: it goes to the data-manual branch, the download uses it as one more copy and the update starts right away.

M. Operations and monitoring → Collectors (Actions, n8n, Peru): Adjusts who fetches what. Every Monday it measures which sources answer from each place and updates the registry the three collectors follow; if the probe has not run in 8 days, the watchdog relaunches it.
N. Website → Operations and monitoring: Checked every 6 hours. Two watchdogs, one on GitHub and one on n8n, check every 6 hours that the site is less than 30 hours old.
O. Operations and monitoring → Daily pipeline: Re-runs or runs by hand. If the site is behind, the watchdog relaunches the update. People also start it when they approve changes or by hand.

P. Publication → Operations and monitoring: Problem alerts. Each problem in the run becomes an alert on GitHub, which closes by itself once the problem goes away; a person closes a format change after checking the values.

Official sources and alerts. What we watch: the ENFEN communiqué, IGP's ICEN, 15 NOAA products and 15 alert services (INDECI, SENAMHI, DHN, IGP, USGS, PTWC and NASA). Also government pages we only keep as an archive.

svg.text: The observatory follows the official ENSO sources (ENFEN, IGP and NOAA), 15 hazard-alert
services and 154 news feeds. It obeys each site's robot rules, except the news feeds it reads
like a feed reader, at most once a day.
At 21:00 a computer in Peru fetches what is blocked, at 22:50 n8n in the cloud keeps a second
copy, and at 23:37 GitHub Actions fetches what it can reach and uses those copies if something
A registry says who fetches what
Some government pages do not answer outside Peru. Every Monday we measure what answers
from where and update a registry that assigns each address to a collector.
If a source does not answer, the Peru or n8n copy, the one an administrator uploaded to the
console, an Internet Archive copy or the last good published value is used. Each value shows its
real date, so nothing old passes as new.
It reads and checks each value, builds the series, reads ENFEN's official status, computes the
GRD signal, filters the news by hazard and places it by department. It logs every problem.
With the site on Cloudflare, when the system is unsure where a news item happened, a
reviewer fixes it in the places console; the fix applies from the next run and stays stored. If no
automatic route brings an official document, an administrator downloads it in their browser and
uploads it in the documents console, and the update starts at once.
All files are built and validated together, the site is tested in a browser and uploaded whole. If
there is a serious problem, yesterday's site stays.
The site shows 10 views, an alert map with the level each agency gave and open downloads,
with links to the original source and the archived copy next to each value. Today's data will be
Two watchdogs check the site every 6 hours; the GitHub one relaunches the update if it falls
behind and warns if a collector goes silent. Each problem becomes a GitHub alert that closes
itself once resolved, except a format change, which a person closes after checking the values.
